    1991 STUART HABER and W. SCOTT STORNETTA propose a chain of digital blocks, each TIME-STAMPED and sealed with CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROOF, to stop digital documents being tampered with. If someone altered a document, the chain would BREAK, instantly exposing the fraud. "The first glimpse of what we now call blockchain"
    1992 MERKLE TREES are added, making verification of large data sets much faster and more secure — "like verifying an entire book's authenticity by checking a few sentences"
    2008 The global financial crisis: banks fail, Lehman Brothers goes bankrupt, savings are lost, markets crash. SATOSHI NAKAMOTO — "we don't know if it is an individual or a group" — publishes the white paper "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System"
    2009 The first Bitcoin block is mined — the GENESIS BLOCK. Over the next year Satoshi mines about a million Bitcoins, then disappears from public view
    2010 Blockchain is still mostly linked to cryptocurrency only
    2015 VITALIK BUTERIN launches ETHEREUM, bringing SMART CONTRACTS — which moved blockchain beyond cryptocurrency into real estate, retail, automotive and more. Enabled DApps (decentralised applications)

    The one powerful question that changed everything: "Can we do things better TOGETHER, WITHOUT relying on the world's guard — the banking systems and the controls we have built?" guaranteed MCQ

    1. Traditional banking vs blockchain guaranteed MCQ
    3

    How a traditional ₹500 transfer works: your request goes to your bank, which checks your account; it goes to your friend's bank, which validates; the amount is updated at both ends. "All this is completely controlled by CENTRAL AUTHORITIES — the banks, the intermediaries, the clearing houses."

    Cross-border is worse: 2 to 3 days minimum, heavy documentation, different time zones, currency fluctuations.

    Dimension Traditional banking Bitcoin / blockchain
    Database CENTRALISED — one authority controls the truth DECENTRALISED — everyone in the network has a copy
    Failure SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE NO single point of failure, no gatekeeper
    On fraud The bank steps in — regulators, insurance, reversals (as in 2008 when the US government intervened) If you lose your PRIVATE KEY, you lose access to your funds. There is NO "reset password" button
    Character Trusted "TRUSTLESS, but UNFORGIVING" — it puts power and responsibility in your hands

    THE RELATIONSHIP TO MEMORISE: guaranteed MCQ

    BLOCKCHAIN is the RAILS (or wheels) of a train. BITCOIN is the TRAIN running on those rails. Bitcoin is the digital MONEY. Blockchain is the TECHNOLOGY that makes it work.

    The Chinese Whispers analogy: in the game the message gets distorted. In blockchain, each person announces loudly what they heard AND provides proof of who told them — that is a BLOCK: a container of transactions, sealed, timestamped and connected to the previous block. "If anyone tries to change one block, every block after it will reject the change." guaranteed MCQ

    1. What blockchain is — the definition and its five properties
    2

    "Blockchain is a DISTRIBUTED LEDGER which allows digital assets to be transacted in REAL TIME, in an IMMUTABLE manner." guaranteed MCQ — the formal definition

    Also described as: "a shared digital notebook that is NOT OWNED BY ANYONE. It lives across thousands of computers. Everyone can see what is written in it, and once something is written, no one can erase or change it."

    THE FIVE CORE PROPERTIES: guaranteed MCQ| # | Property | Meaning and example | |---|---|---| | 1 | PEER-TO-PEER — no middleman | A cross-border transfer normally needs 3–4 institutions: your bank, a currency processor, an intermediate bank, the destination bank. Blockchain removes them | | 2 | DISTRIBUTED LEDGER | "Imagine every time you bought something, EVERYONE IN THE STORE instantly got a copy of your receipt." Every node gets the same record at the same time | | 3 | IMMUTABILITY | Once recorded, it is permanent. The hospital example: a blood test showing HbA1c 5.8 cannot be altered to 7.3. A land record cannot be forged | | 4 | TRANSPARENCY | "You could open a file and see where every rupee came from, where it went and why." You don't need to TRUST the system — you can VERIFY it yourself | | 5 | PROGRAMMABILITY via SMART CONTRACTS | The VENDING MACHINE analogy: insert ₹100, press a button, the machine gives you chips/biscuits/chocolate. No person involved — just rules written in code | | (+) | SECURITY | Each block is linked to the one before it "like a digital spine". Because it is not stored in one place, hackers would have to hack ALL the computers/nodes |

    Blockchain use cases he names: FARM TO FORK (tracing fish from the sea/river to your plate — where caught, cleaning, preparation, cooking) · finance (decentralised lending, tokenised assets, KYC, CBDC) · healthcare (patient data, patient-controlled consent) · plus Bitcoin and Ethereum themselves.

    1. The FOUR types of blockchain guaranteed MCQ — the whole table
    2

    The analogy: different types of ROADS — highways, private lanes, express highways.

    Type Analogy Who can join / control Platforms Use cases
    PUBLIC A TOWN HALL MEETING — anyone can walk in, listen, speak, vote Anyone can join, anyone can view; NO ONE is in charge. Verified by Proof of Work / Proof of Stake Bitcoin, Ethereum Peer-to-peer payments, smart contracts, DApps; builds trust WITHOUT any central authority
    PRIVATE A COMPANY MEETING — you need an ID card to get past security Only selected, permissioned people can read or write; usually controlled by a SINGLE organisation Hyperledger Fabric, Enterprise Ethereum Internal banking systems, supply chain tracking (the farm-to-fork hotel inviting its vendors), secure inter-departmental data sharing, trade finance. Faster, because fewer participants
    CONSORTIUM A CLOSED-DOOR INDUSTRY MEETING Controlled by a GROUP (e.g. five insurance companies together), not one company and not the public R3 Corda, IBM Food Trust Trusted partnerships; e.g. exporting mangoes from Indian farms to US supermarkets
    HYBRID A UNIVERSITY PORTAL — courses and faculty are public; your marks and attendance are private Mix of public and private — "smart privacy" IBM Food Trust Healthcare (public guidelines vs private patient records), government land registry (open to view, personal owner details protected), real estate, artwork trading

    The closing principle: "It is NOT about which one is better; it is about WHICH USE CASE you are trying to solve." guaranteed MCQ

    1. NODES — the four types guaranteed MCQ
    2

    A NODE is simply a computer connected to the blockchain network — "a corporate data centre, or a laptop in someone's bedroom." Each node holds a copy of the blockchain.

    What nodes do: store the data · verify new transactions · share information with other nodes · reject anything suspicious.

    The shared-Excel analogy: a change (cell A4 from 23 to 46) is broadcast to everyone; only if the MAJORITY agree does the update happen; otherwise it is rejected.

    # Node type Role
    1 FULL NODE Stores the ENTIRE history of the blockchain from day one. "Like a library that has every edition of every book ever written." Validates every transaction, checks signatures, enforces rules. Even if 99% of the network disappears, as long as ONE full node survives, you have the entire data guaranteed MCQ
    2 MINER NODE A full node with an extra job — solving complex mathematical puzzles to ADD NEW BLOCKS. "Security guards and bricklayers at the same time." Rewarded in cryptocurrency
    3 LIGHT / PARTIAL NODE Does NOT store the full blockchain — relies on full nodes. Keeps recent data for balances and simple verification. "Like someone reading just the latest news." Example: your mobile crypto app, or DHL in a supply chain holding only logistics-related information
    4 MASTER NODE An advanced full node that does NOT mine. Takes on governance, monitoring and backups, ensuring the network runs smoothly and stays online. Requires STAKING some crypto as a deposit — so there are usually only one or two

    The WhatsApp-group analogy for node communication: someone posts a message; every member checks whether it is real and follows the group rules; only then is it accepted — but with NO group admin.

    1. CONSENSUS MECHANISMS guaranteed MCQ
    6

    The question consensus answers: "If NO ONE is in charge, how does the system agree on what is TRUE?"

    The restaurant-bill analogy: friends splitting a bill must agree on the total even though no one is officially in charge. Now imagine that with thousands of strangers across the world.

    7.1 PROOF OF WORK — "the puzzle game"

    • The ORIGINAL consensus mechanism. Bitcoin runs on it (and early Ethereum)
    • Miners compete to solve a very complex mathematical puzzle — "a digital lottery, but instead of buying tickets they BURN ELECTRICITY"
    • Whoever solves it FIRST gets to add the next block and earns a reward
    • The key asymmetry: the puzzle is VERY HARD TO SOLVE but EASY FOR EVERYONE ELSE TO VERIFY guaranteed MCQ
    • To cheat, you would have to redo all that work across thousands of blocks — "like rewriting the entire history of the internet in real time"
    Pros Cons
    Extremely secure; tried and tested — Bitcoin has run for at least 15 years · rewards miners' effort and infrastructure Huge energy consumption · expensive hardware · CAN BECOME CENTRALISED, because only those who can afford it can participate — "which somewhere negates what blockchain was brought in for"

    7.2 PROOF OF STAKE — "skin in the game"

    • Instead of burning energy, you use your MONEY. To participate you STAKE some coins like a security deposit
    • Play fair → earn rewards. Try to cheat → LOSE YOUR STAKE
    • "It's like saying: I believe this block is valid, and I'm willing to bet my own money on it"
    • The network randomly chooses VALIDATORS from those who have staked

    THE TWO STYLES OF PROOF OF STAKE: guaranteed MCQ 1. CHAIN-BASED PoS — ONE validator is selected per time slot to create the next block, pointing to the previous one 2. BFT-STYLE PoS — MULTIPLE validators VOTE IN ROUNDS to agree on a valid block. "A bit like JURY DUTY in court"

    Pros Cons
    Energy efficient · lower entry cost · faster and more scalable Not as strongly secure as PoW · security depends on economic assumptions · risk that rich players gain too much influence

    7.3 The comparison and the metaphor guaranteed MCQ

    PROOF OF WORK is like BUILDING A FORT WITH STONES in the olden ages — hard and time-consuming, but extremely strong. PROOF OF STAKE is like a modern SMART BUILDING WITH SENSORS — fast and efficient, but it needs strict rules and oversight, otherwise it can fail.

    Who uses what: Bitcoin stays with PoW because it values SECURITY above all. Ethereum MOVED from PoW to PoS to scale, save energy and build more applications. Cardano, Solana and Polygon also use PoS. guaranteed MCQ The takeaway: "Consensus mechanisms are not just technical features — they represent the VALUES AND PRIORITIES of the network."

    And the security threshold: to cheat, a node would need to "convince MORE THAN 50% of the nodes of the entire network." guaranteed MCQ

    1. MINING — the process guaranteed MCQ — the five steps
    5

    Mining does THREE key things: guaranteed MCQ 1. Secures the network 2. Keeps the system DECENTRALISED 3. Ensures trust WITHOUT a central authority

    Step What happens
    1. Transaction is BROADCAST "Alice wants to send 2 Bitcoins to Bob." Every node sees it as pending
    2. Miners BUNDLE transactions into a BLOCK Hundreds or thousands of pending transactions from the last 5–10 minutes. "Like collecting receipts in one big folder"
    3. PUZZLE SOLVING (proof of work) Miners compete to find a specific number called a HASH that meets certain rules — "like playing digital Sudoku with millions of combinations." Energy-intensive: a single Bitcoin block can use as much electricity as a small town
    4. BLOCK VERIFICATION (peer validation) The solution is broadcast; other miners check did the answer meet the rules? did the block include valid transactions? If yes → added; if no → rejected
    5. REWARD The winning miner gets the BLOCK REWARD (new coins) PLUS the TRANSACTION FEES from users

    8.1 What is INSIDE a block guaranteed MCQ

    The transactions · the TIMESTAMP · the PREVIOUS BLOCK'S HASH · a special number called the NONCE · a measure of DIFFICULTY · and the MERKLE ROOT.

    8.2 The MERKLE TREE guaranteed MCQ

    Each transaction is turned into a hash. Pairs of hashes are combined and hashed again. This keeps going until you have a SINGLE HASH AT THE TOP — the MERKLE ROOT. If even ONE transaction inside the block changes, the MERKLE ROOT COMPLETELY CHANGES. "It's like a digital fingerprint — a tiny change gives a totally different fingerprint."

    8.3 The sustainability problem guaranteed MCQ

    "Bitcoin alone consumes more energy annually than some countries — countries like DENMARK actually consume LESS electricity than the whole Bitcoin network." This is a key reason many blockchains are shifting to PROOF OF STAKE.

    The closing metaphor: "Mining is like the engine of early blockchain systems — like a STEAM or COAL ENGINE: powerful, but it uses a lot of fuel. We now want engines just as strong, but cleaner, faster and greener."

    1. How a blockchain transaction works — the seven steps guaranteed MCQ
    2

    Step Detail
    1. Create the transaction A digital cheque containing: my public address · the recipient's public address · the amount · MY DIGITAL SIGNATURE — "this ensures only I could have initiated it"
    2. Broadcast to the network Sent to thousands of nodes; sits in a pool waiting for verification. "Like shouting in a crowded room"
    3. Reach CONSENSUS Nodes check: do I really have 2 Bitcoins? Is the digital signature valid? Have those coins already been spent elsewhere? via PoW, PoS or BFT
    4. Create the block Validated transactions grouped, with the timestamp, the previous block's hash, and its own unique hash
    5. HASHING "Generating a fingerprint of the data. Even a tiny change — 2 Bitcoins → 2.1 Bitcoins — creates a completely different hash, breaking the link." It's like sealing every page in a notebook
    6. MERKLE TREE inside the block Summarises all transactions into the Merkle root
    7. Add block + UPDATE THE LEDGER across the network Every participant updates their copy → a SINGLE VERSION OF TRUTH across the globe

    The online-exam analogy: "You submit answers (the transaction) → the system broadcasts to proctors worldwide (the nodes) → they verify (consensus) → answers are locked into a master file (a block) → linked to all previous submissions (the blockchain) → the entire class gets a copy (the distributed ledger)." guaranteed MCQ

    1. Benefits, limitations and MYTHS guaranteed MCQ
    4

    10.1 Benefits

    TRANSPARENCY · IMMUTABILITY · NO INTERMEDIARIES (lower cost, faster transactions, access for people without formal financial services — "remote villages that don't have banks").

    10.2 Limitations — with the numbers guaranteed MCQ| Limitation | Detail |

    |---|---| | SCALABILITY | Bitcoin handles around 7 TRANSACTIONS PER SECOND. VISA does 24,000+. "Not yet built for high-volume, real-time global commerce" | | ENERGY USE | PoW mining consumes massive electricity — more than Denmark | | REGULATORY UNCERTAINTY | Laws around blockchain, crypto and digital identity are still evolving; different countries have different rules or none at all |

    10.3 The three trade-offs guaranteed MCQ

    More TRUST, but less SPEED · more DECENTRALISATION, but more COMPLEXITY · more TRANSPARENCY, but less PRIVACY. "Blockchain is not a magic wand. You cannot hit a mosquito with a hammer."

    10.4 THE THREE MYTHS guaranteed MCQ — expect a "which of the following is TRUE/FALSE" question| Myth | Reality |

    |---|---| | "Blockchain is just Bitcoin" | FALSE. "Bitcoin is like EMAIL; blockchain is the whole INTERNET that makes email and thousands of other things possible." Blockchain powers supply chains (Walmart, Maersk), trade finance, healthcare records (Estonia), land registries (Andhra Pradesh), voting platforms (US) | | "Blockchain is just crypto" | FALSE. "You can have a blockchain WITHOUT ANY TOKENS at all" — hospital consent tracking, government land digitisation, on permissioned blockchains with NO crypto. "Crypto is one application of blockchain, just as social media is one application of the internet" | | "Blockchain is ANONYMOUS" | FALSE — it is PSEUDONYMOUS. "Your NAME is not shown, but your PUBLIC ADDRESS is known to everyone. Every transaction is permanently recorded and open for anyone to see. Over time your address CAN BE LINKED to your identity, especially if you use exchanges, wallets or banks (KYC). It is not invisible — it is TRACEABLE with enough data." |

    1. Cryptocurrency and crypto trading
    14

    11.1 What cryptocurrency is guaranteed MCQ

    Digital money that — unlike Paytm or UPI — is NOT issued by a government or bank. It is secured by CRYPTOGRAPHY and runs on blockchain networks. There is no physical coin and no account number, just a combination of PUBLIC and PRIVATE KEYS.

    Origin: 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto's white paper — a response to the financial crisis; a vision of money that is peer-to-peer, borderless and independent of banks.

    The crucial contrast: "Unlike your bank account where only the BANK knows your balance, in crypto the ENTIRE NETWORK agrees on your balance and no single party can change it." guaranteed MCQ

    11.2 How a crypto transaction flows guaranteed MCQ

    Open wallet → enter the recipient's alphanumeric address → SIGN with your PRIVATE KEY ("like signing a cheque, but with cryptography") → broadcast → it lands in the MEMORY POOL ("a temporary waiting area for UNCONFIRMED transactions") → miners/validators verify and add it to a block via PoW/PoS → the recipient's wallet shows the balance.

    11.3 The named cryptocurrencies guaranteed MCQ — match name to purpose| Coin | Purpose |

    |---|---| | BITCOIN | The original crypto; a store of value — "digital gold". Limited supply: ONLY 21 MILLION will ever exist guaranteed MCQ| | ETHEREUM | A PLATFORM for smart contracts and DApps; powers most of DeFi and the NFT ecosystem | | USDT (Tether) | A STABLECOIN pegged to the US dollar, used by traders to avoid volatility | | RIPPLE (XRP) | Designed for fast, low-cost INTERNATIONAL PAYMENTS between banks; enterprise focus | | CARDANO | Proof-of-stake blockchain focused on research and sustainability; competes with Ethereum |

    11.4 Scale and adoption facts guaranteed MCQ

    Bitcoin has a market cap of hundreds of billions · Ethereum powers DeFi and NFTs · EL SALVADOR made Bitcoin LEGAL TENDER · roughly 400 MILLION people globally own some form of cryptocurrency · in India crypto is NOT ILLEGAL, but is TAXED AND REGULATED.

    11.5 The four types of STABLECOIN guaranteed MCQ| Type | Backing | Example |

    |---|---|---| | FIAT-BACKED | Actual dollars in a bank | USDC, USDT | | CRYPTO-BACKED | Other crypto (e.g. Ethereum), OVER-COLLATERALISED | DAI | | ALGORITHMIC | Supply algorithms maintain the price | Frax | | COMMODITY-BACKED | Real gold, iron ore, copper | PAX Gold (PAXG) |

    "Fiat-backed and crypto-backed are MORE famous than algorithmic and commodity-backed." Stablecoins are used for trading pairs on DEXs, as COLLATERAL in lending platforms, and for saving/remitting without volatility. They are "the BRIDGE between traditional currency and volatile crypto." guaranteed MCQ

    11.6 Utility vs security tokens guaranteed MCQ| | UTILITY TOKEN | SECURITY TOKEN |

    |---|---|---| | Grants | ACCESS to a product or service | OWNERSHIP or PROFIT RIGHTS — "digital shares" |

    11.7 Crypto trading — the three types guaranteed MCQ| Type | Description |

    |---|---| | SPOT trading | Buy Bitcoin today at ₹25 lakh, hold or sell for profit. "Simple, like buying gold." Start here if you're a beginner | | FUTURES trading | Agree to buy or sell later at a fixed price — more speculative | | MARGIN trading | BORROW money to take a bigger position — risky; gains AND losses are amplified |

    Market characteristics: 24×7, global, fast and VOLATILE. Participants: retail investors, institutions, BOTS and exchanges.

    Platforms named: BINANCE (global giant, advanced tools) · COINDCX and WAZIRX (popular in India, beginner-friendly) · COINBASE (US-based, regulated, clean UI). guaranteed MCQ Key market indicators: MARKET CAP (= price × number of coins) · VOLUME · BITCOIN DOMINANCE (how much of the total market Bitcoin controls — currently high, but altcoins are rising). guaranteed MCQ

    11.8 CRYPTO WALLETS — the most examinable block guaranteed MCQ

    A wallet does NOT hold coins the way a leather wallet holds cash. IT HOLDS THE PRIVATE KEYS. Your cryptocurrency is NOT on your phone or computer — it is ON THE BLOCKCHAIN LEDGER. The wallet holds the keys that let you unlock and move those funds.

    Key Analogy
    PUBLIC KEY Like your UPI ID or account number — you SHARE it
    PRIVATE KEY Like your ATM PIN — you NEVER share it
    SEED PHRASE A MASTER PASSWORD — a backup that can recover everything

    "If you lose your private key or seed phrase, your funds are GONE. There is no 'forgot password' button in crypto. That is the price of decentralisation." guaranteed MCQ| | HOT WALLET | COLD WALLET | |---|---|---| | Connection | Connected to the internet | OFFLINE storage | | Examples | MetaMask, Trust Wallet, exchange wallets | A USB device, or even PAPER — Ledger, Trezor | | Trade-off | Convenient but MORE EXPOSED to online threats | Safer from hacking; ideal for LONG-TERM holding | | Analogy | Your digital CHECKING ACCOUNT | Your VAULT at home where you keep gold and critical documents |

    1. SMART CONTRACTS guaranteed MCQ
    6

    12.1 Definition and history

    "A piece of CODE on the blockchain that runs AUTOMATICALLY when the agreed conditions are met." No lawyers, no signatures, no stamps, no reminders, no approvals, no delays.

    HISTORY: first proposed in 1994 by NICK SZABO, a cryptographer and computer scientist. They became popular in 2015 with the launch of ETHEREUM. guaranteed MCQ

    12.2 The four properties

    TRANSPARENT (everyone can see the rules) · IMMUTABLE (once deployed, cannot be changed) · NO MIDDLEMAN · EFFICIENT (reduces admin errors and delays).

    12.3 The four steps to deploy guaranteed MCQ

    1. Define the TERMS (what needs to happen, when, who is involved) → 2. Convert them into CODE (developers turn them into logical statements) → 3. DEPLOY on the blockchain → 4. AUTOMATIC EXECUTION when conditions are met.

    12.4 The real-world use cases guaranteed MCQ| Use case | How it works |

    |---|---| | LENDING AND BORROWING (platforms Aave and Compound) | You deposit crypto as COLLATERAL; the contract checks the value and approves the loan; repay on time and the collateral is automatically released; miss payments and the contract AUTOMATICALLY LIQUIDATES the assets. No banks, no credit checks, no paperwork | | INSURANCE | Flight delay insurance: the contract is connected to real-time flight data through ORACLES. If your flight is delayed by more than 2 hours, it automatically pays you ₹5,000 — no claim forms, no phone calls | | PAYMENTS | Recurring salary payments, vendor payouts after delivery, bonus distribution after targets are met — every payment is condition-based | | TRADE FINANCE | Document verification, payment settlement, letter-of-credit processing |

    12.5 THE FOUR LIMITATIONS AND RISKS guaranteed MCQ| Risk | Detail |

    |---|---| | LEGAL UNCERTAINTY | Smart contracts may not be legally recognised in courts. "If something goes wrong, who do you sue? THE CODE?" | | CODE BUGS | THE DAO HACK, 2016 — a flaw in the smart contract allowed $60 MILLION worth of Ether to be drained. "In smart contracts, CODE IS LAW. If there is a bug, it can be exploited" guaranteed MCQ| | DEPENDENCY ON ORACLES | If the oracle fails or gives wrong data (e.g. reports the flight was on time when it was delayed), the contract behaves incorrectly | | INFLEXIBILITY | Once deployed it cannot be edited — "great for trust, but bad for flexibility when business rules change frequently", unlike SAP or Oracle where you just change it |

    The future direction: regulatory alignment (governments exploring digital contract law) · hybrid models (smart contracts + traditional finance + KYC compliance) · cross-chain support (Ethereum, Polygon, Solana) · AI-powered contracts adapting terms based on real-time data.

    1. ORACLES guaranteed MCQ
    6

    "Smart contracts CANNOT SEE THE REAL WORLD. A BLOCKCHAIN ORACLE is the BRIDGE between the blockchain world and the real world — it feeds external data into smart contracts so they can execute based on live inputs." "Think of an oracle as an API for smart contracts." "If smart contracts are the BRAINS, oracles are the EYES AND EARS." guaranteed MCQ The two triggering examples: crop insurance payout if RAINFALL IS BELOW 50 mm; a DeFi loan if the ETH PRICE IS ABOVE $2,000. guaranteed MCQ The DeFi flow: the contract requests the ETH/USD price → the oracle fetches it from MULTIPLE external sources → the verified data is written to the blockchain → the contract executes (approving a loan, issuing a payout, triggering liquidation).

    13.1 THE FIVE TYPES OF ORACLE guaranteed MCQ| Type | Function |

    |---|---| | SOFTWARE oracles | Fetch digital data — price feeds, weather, APIs | | HARDWARE oracles | Pull info from IoT devices or SENSORS — "very much used in supply chain, e.g. controlling TEMPERATURES for trucks carrying pharmaceuticals" | | INBOUND oracles | Bring external data INTO the blockchain | | OUTBOUND oracles | Send blockchain results OUT to the world | | CONSENSUS-BASED oracles | Use MULTIPLE data sources to reduce manipulation risk |

    The big oracle providers: CHAINLINK (the most widely used in DeFi) · BAND PROTOCOL (fast, scalable, cross-chain) · API3 (lets data providers run their own oracles). guaranteed MCQ The India example: an insurance oracle might pull rainfall data from the IMD (INDIAN METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT) to automatically trigger payouts on a smart crop policy. guaranteed MCQ

    1. GAS guaranteed MCQ
    3

    "Not the fuel for your scooter — the FUEL FOR YOUR TRANSACTIONS on blockchains like Ethereum. Every action — sending a token, executing a smart contract, minting an NFT — requires computational power. GAS is the UNIT USED TO MEASURE THIS." "Think of it like ELECTRICITY UNITS ON A METER. The more complex the operation, the more gas it consumes."

    Why it costs money: validators use their own hardware and electricity. Gas fees prevent network spam, pay validators, and help Ethereum stay secure and sustainable.

    14.1 THE THREE PARTS OF A GAS FEE guaranteed MCQ| Part | Meaning |

    |---|---| | GAS LIMIT | The MAXIMUM gas you are willing to spend | | BASE FEE | Set by network demand — and it is BURNED, NOT PAID TO ANYONE guaranteed MCQ| | PRIORITY FEE | A TIP to get faster processing — high demand means higher fees |

    "Smart contract developers work hard to OPTIMISE THE CODE TO USE LESS GAS — the more optimisation, the less gas used, so it becomes cost-effective."

    1. DECENTRALISED FINANCE (DeFi) guaranteed MCQ
    15

    15.1 The definition

    "An emerging PEER-TO-PEER financial system that uses BLOCKCHAIN and CRYPTOCURRENCIES to allow people, businesses or other entities to transact DIRECTLY with each other."

    No branches, no customer service calls, no approvals — just code on smart contracts. Built on PUBLIC blockchains like Ethereum. Three headline benefits: ACCESS for anyone with a phone and internet · TRANSPARENCY of every transaction · services that run 24×7.

    15.2 THE FIVE PILLARS OF DeFi guaranteed MCQ — memorise the list

    1. DECENTRALISED EXCHANGES (DEX) · 2. STABLECOINS · 3. LENDING AND BORROWING · 4. ASSET MANAGEMENT · 5. DERIVATIVES

    15.3 Pillar 1 — DECENTRALISED EXCHANGES

    Unlike a centralised exchange (WazirX, Binance), a DEX like UNISWAP runs entirely on blockchain. NO COMPANY HOLDS YOUR FUNDS — you connect your wallet and trade directly with the protocol. guaranteed MCQ THE KEY MECHANISM — AMM (AUTOMATED MARKET MAKER): guaranteed MCQ

    A smart contract that REPLACES THE ORDER BOOK. Instead of matching buyers and sellers, AMMs use LIQUIDITY POOLS. Users deposit tokens into these pools and in return EARN A SHARE OF TRADING FEES.

    The MAKER–TAKER flow: guaranteed MCQ 1. The MAKER creates a new trade order (e.g. sell Ethereum for USDC) 2. The maker DIGITALLY SIGNS the order using their PRIVATE KEY — proving ownership 3. The order is sent to the blockchain, visible to the entire network — public, traceable, tamper-proof 4. The TAKER accepts the offer, adds their signature, and the SMART CONTRACT automatically validates 5. Funds are instantly transferred between wallets

    The named DEX: UNISWAP, built on Ethereum — permissionless, open source, used by millions. The three named risks: SLIPPAGE · SMART CONTRACT BUGS · IMPERMANENT LOSS. guaranteed MCQ

    15.4 Pillar 2 — STABLECOINS (see §11.5 for the four types)

    The volatility problem he illustrates: "Imagine your rent is ₹40,000 and overnight it becomes ₹80,000 — that's crypto. One message from the US or China can send it up or down."

    15.5 Pillar 3 — LENDING AND BORROWING guaranteed MCQ

    In traditional finance you need credit scores, paperwork, collateral and bank approval. THE INSTRUCTOR'S OWN STORY: an SBI credit card closed in 2009 left ₹133 unpaid; nine years later that ₹133 wrecked his credit score and he was REFUSED A ₹1 CRORE LOAN. guaranteed MCQ — this anecdote appears twice in the course In DeFi you just need a WALLET and some COLLATERAL. Worked example on AAVE: lock up $10,000 of Ethereum → borrow $6,000 of USDC INSTANTLY, WITHOUT SHOWING ANY ID. guaranteed MCQ Aave's three named features: guaranteed MCQ - FLASH LOANS — "borrow money WITHOUT COLLATERAL for a few seconds" - RATE SWITCHING — move between fixed and floating interest - GOVERNANCE TOKENS — Aave holders VOTE on how the protocol runs

    Benefits: passive income · instant liquidity · operate without banks. Risks: LIQUIDATION if crypto prices crash · SMART CONTRACT BUGS · NO GOVERNMENT BAILOUTS.

    15.6 Pillar 4 — DERIVATIVES guaranteed MCQ

    Contracts whose value is based on an underlying asset, but running on blockchain and smart contracts. Platforms: SYNTHETIX and dYdX — allowing users to trade SYNTHETIC ASSETS, on-chain versions of real-world assets including stocks, indices and commodities. Smart contracts replace brokers, clearing houses and paperwork, executing trades, managing risk and settling contracts instantly.

    15.7 Pillar 5 — ASSET MANAGEMENT guaranteed MCQ

    Platforms: YEARN FINANCE and IDLE FINANCE. They scan the whole DeFi market and move your funds to the HIGHEST-YIELDING opportunities in real time — "like having a ROBO-ADVISOR, but running on blockchain 24×7 with full transparency." Users can earn interest by lending tokens, AUTO-SWITCH to better rates across DeFi protocols, and participate in YIELD FARMING without managing it manually.

    DeFi management platforms: INSTADAPP — "a DASHBOARD for decentralised finance" managing loans, swaps, collaterals and leverage across Aave, MakerDAO and Compound in one place — and it was BUILT BY INDIAN DEVELOPERS. Its features: smart wallet routing · one-click refinancing · gas optimisation · institutional-level UX. guaranteed MCQ Other DeFi use cases: INSURANCE — NEXUS MUTUAL provides coverage against smart contract hacks; and SAVINGS TOOLS — earn yield by depositing stablecoins. guaranteed MCQ

    1. CROSS-BORDER PAYMENTS guaranteed MCQ
    13

    17.1 Definition

    "Financial transactions between individuals, businesses or financial institutions located in DIFFERENT COUNTRIES, involving the transfer of funds or assets ACROSS NATIONAL BORDERS and often involving DIFFERENT CURRENCIES."

    17.2 The SIX steps of a cross-border payment guaranteed MCQ

    1. Choose a payment method (bank, PayPal, Western Union) → 2. Check the EXCHANGE RATE → 3. Enter the RECIPIENT'S DETAILS (name, bank account, country, sometimes a local ID) → 4. VERIFY the payment → 5. CONFIRM AND SEND → 6. TRACK the payment "just like tracking a parcel"

    17.3 The traditional correspondent-banking chain guaranteed MCQ

    Kotak Bank (India) → CENTRAL BANK in India (RBI) → CORRESPONDENT BANK in India (SBI/HSBC/American Express) → CORRESPONDENT BANK in the US → CENTRAL BANK in the US → Chase Bank (the recipient's bank) Costs: lifting charges · FOREX conversion fees · operational cost at each step. Time: 2–3 days, up to 5 days. Tracking: LIMITED — "the sender doesn't know where the money is during the journey."

    17.4 THE SEVEN CHALLENGES of traditional cross-border payments guaranteed MCQ

    1. UNPREDICTABLE FEES · 2. CURRENCY FLUCTUATIONS · 3. PAYMENT DELAYS (3–5 days or more) · 4. EXHAUSTIVE DOCUMENTATION (for AML checks) · 5. HIDDEN CHARGES · 6. COMMUNICATION BARRIERS (time zones, languages) · 7. TRUST ISSUES (multiple banks and middlemen).

    17.5 THE MARKET NUMBERS guaranteed MCQ| Statistic | Figure |

    |---|---| | Blockchain-based cross-border payments as a share of the market (2021) | nearly 16% of the $4.67 billion market | | Overall blockchain market growth | from $27 BILLION in 2024 to over $800 BILLION by 2032 |

    17.6 Why blockchain fixes it guaranteed MCQ

    FAST (minutes, not days) · SECURE · TRANSPARENT (track your money at every step) · CHEAPER (no middlemen, no hidden costs).

    "It is like UPI, but for INTERNATIONAL transfers." guaranteed MCQ The domestic analogy he draws: NEFT through a bank may take an hour, has cut-off times and holiday restrictions — "that's like traditional cross-border payments." UPI is instant, super easy, no extra charges — that is what blockchain is trying to do for international payments.

    17.7 The two blockchain models guaranteed MCQ

    MODEL 1 — DIRECT PEER-TO-PEER (A to B): A creates a block with transaction details (amount, sender, receiver, time) → the block is verified by the network of computers worldwide → the block is added to the blockchain → money moves from A to B. No banks in between.

    MODEL 2 — CROSS-BORDER THROUGH BANKS (the bigger revolution): Kotak Bank completes KYC and receives the deposit in fiat (INR) → a SMART CONTRACT is created → the transaction flows through the DLT (DISTRIBUTED LEDGER TECHNOLOGY) NETWORK → FOREIGN EXCHANGE is handled WITHIN the blockchain system via smart contracts and DLT → the money reaches the US bank, which verifies KYC and disburses → REGULATORS (the FEDERAL RESERVE and the RESERVE BANK OF INDIA) can MONITOR the transaction through the blockchain WITHOUT SLOWING IT DOWN. guaranteed MCQ

    17.8 Blockchain vs traditional — the six-row comparison guaranteed MCQ| Dimension | BLOCKCHAIN-BASED | TRADITIONAL |

    |---|---|---| | Central authorities | None — banks involved only for KYC | Many banks and middlemen | | Access | 24×7 | Limited to banking days and hours | | Fees | LOW | HIGH | | Speed | Minutes | 4 hours to 5 days | | KYC/AML | Business transactions only | Required for ALL transactions | | Immutability | 100% tamper-proof | Changes possible with system access |

    17.9 The AXIS BANK–RIPPLENET use case guaranteed MCQ

    The five steps: 1. A customer approaches Axis Bank to send money abroad → 2. Axis connects with the receiver's bank via RIPPLENET and asks for a QUOTE (exchange rate and fees) → 3. Both banks do KYC and compliance checks → 4. Money is transferred using RippleNet → 5. Both banks get confirmation and the customer is notified.

    17.10 THE FIVE WAYS BLOCKCHAIN IMPROVES BANK-TO-BANK PAYMENTS guaranteed MCQ

    1. Replaces older systems like SWIFT with INSTANT COMMUNICATION between banks · 2. Payments settle ALMOST INSTANTLY · 3. PRE-VALIDATION catches mistakes like wrong account numbers BEFORE the payment is processed · 4. Fewer intermediaries → lower fees · 5. GLOBAL INTEROPERABILITY — even banks not directly connected can work together.

    "Blockchain makes bank-to-bank payments work like WHATSAPP CHATS — fast, clear and direct."

    1. CBDC — CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY guaranteed MCQ
    20

    18.1 Definition

    "A DIGITAL FORM of a country's FIAT CURRENCY, ISSUED AND REGULATED BY THE CENTRAL BANK." "It is NOT a cryptocurrency like Bitcoin, which is private and decentralised. CBDC is CENTRALISED, LEGAL TENDER and GOVERNMENT-BACKED."

    The THREE main goals: MODERNISE the payment system · promote FINANCIAL INCLUSION · REDUCE DEPENDENCE ON PHYSICAL CASH. guaranteed MCQ

    18.2 THE TWO TYPES guaranteed MCQ| Type | For whom |

    |---|---| | RETAIL CBDC | The general public — groceries, paying friends, shopping online via a mobile wallet | | WHOLESALE CBDC | Banks and large financial institutions — faster interbank settlements, reducing cost and risk |

    18.3 THE SIX REASONS COUNTRIES ARE EXPLORING CBDC guaranteed MCQ

    1. CASH IS DYING (people prefer UPI-style contactless payments) · 2. TRANSPARENCY (track money flow, reduce black money) · 3. MONETARY CONTROL (as private stablecoins grow) · 4. COST SAVINGS (no printing, storing or transporting cash) · 5. FINANCIAL INCLUSION (rural users without bank access can use CBDC via mobile wallets) · 6. FASTER PAYMENTS (instant, 24×7, domestic and eventually cross-border).

    India's pilot: the e-RUPEE / DIGITAL RUPEE. China is testing its DIGITAL YUAN at large scale. guaranteed MCQ

    18.4 THE FIVE KEY FEATURES guaranteed MCQ

    PRIVACY ("like cash it can offer anonymity TO SOME EXTENT, not fully") · TRANSFERABILITY (person to person like UPI) · CONVENIENCE ("you don't need a bank — your mobile wallet is enough") · ACCESSIBILITY (reaches remote areas) · FINANCIAL SECURITY (backed by the RBI).

    "It combines the TRUST OF CASH with the SPEED OF DIGITAL."

    18.8 How CBDC works — the six steps guaranteed MCQ

    1. The RBI ISSUES the CBDC (creates the e-Rupee) — "just like RBI printing cash, but digital" → 2. DISTRIBUTED VIA BANKS OR WALLET APPS (commercial banks or authorised providers like PhonePe, Paytm, Google Pay) — "they act like ATMs" → 3. The user STORES IT IN A DIGITAL WALLET — NOT in a savings account → 4. PAY by scanning a QR code or entering a mobile number — "like handing over ₹500 cash" → 5. NO BANK PERMISSION NEEDED — OFFLINE payments possible via Bluetooth or NFC → 6. Every transaction is RECORDED on a secure, transparent system for fraud detection and compliance, but SMALL-VALUE payments can still be private like cash.

INTERMEDIARY | RBI issues the CBDC and passes it to INTERMEDIARIES — commercial banks (SBI, HDFC, ICICI) or payment apps (Paytm, Google Pay) — who distribute it to individuals and merchants | THE MODEL INDIA IS CURRENTLY TESTING. Easier to roll out, uses existing infrastructure; slight complexity in control and privacy guaranteed MCQ| | 3. HYBRID | RBI keeps FULL CONTROL of the currency and the LEDGER, but customer interaction is handled by intermediaries. The user still has a DIRECT CLAIM ON THE RBI even though a private player operates the app | Combines RBI's trust with private-sector innovation. "India is most probably looking at model 2 or 3 — still not finalised" |

    18.10 The CBDC lifecycle on blockchain — three steps guaranteed MCQ

    1. ISSUANCE / MINTING: deposit ₹500, receive ₹500 in e-Rupee in your wallet — fully recorded on the blockchain 2. TRANSFER: every transfer (person-to-person or person-to-merchant) is recorded on the blockchain network — tamper-proof, secure, traceable 3. REDEMPTION: ₹200 of e-Rupee is removed from the wallet and credited to your savings account — again validated on the blockchain

    The corporate example: a large company (e.g. Reliance) pays HUNDREDS OF SUPPLIERS INSTANTLY — the company requests the transaction on the blockchain, the bank approves, the CBDC moves to each supplier's wallet, the central bank verifies, and ALL PARTIES INCLUDING REGULATORS CAN SEE IT. Processing time drops from DAYS TO SECONDS. guaranteed MCQ

    1. TRADE FINANCE guaranteed MCQ

    19.1 Definition

    "The financial INSTRUMENTS and PRODUCTS that are used to FACILITATE INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND COMMERCE."

    Why it matters: it REDUCES RISK for both exporter and importer · helps companies trade globally even when they don't know each other well · provides CREDIT, GUARANTEES AND INSURANCE.

    19.2 THE SIX STAKEHOLDERS guaranteed MCQ| # | Stakeholder | Role |

    |---|---|---| | 1 | BANKS | The heart of the system — provide financing, guarantees and letters of credit. Example: Pai Electronics buys gadgets from Japan; SBI provides the LC ensuring the Japanese exporter is paid once goods are shipped | | 2 | IMPORTERS AND EXPORTERS | The main users — need payments, risk protection and credit support | | 3 | EXPORT CREDIT AGENCIES (ECAs) | Government-supported institutions providing LOAN GUARANTEES or INSURANCE to exporters. In India: the ECGC — EXPORT CREDIT GUARANTEE CORPORATION | | 4 | MULTILATERAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS (MDBs) | The WORLD BANK, ASIAN DEVELOPMENT BANK — step in when private banks are hesitant, especially in developing countries or high-risk regions | | 5 | INSURERS | Provide TRADE CREDIT INSURANCE protecting exporters against bankruptcy, political risk or currency restrictions | | 6 | GOVERNMENTS AND REGULATORS | Make policies, set regulations, negotiate trade agreements |

    "The trade finance system is like a TEAM SPORT."

    19.3 THE FOUR KEY DOCUMENTS guaranteed MCQ| Document | Definition |

    |---|---| | LETTER OF CREDIT (LC) | "A GUARANTEE FROM A BANK that the exporter will be paid ONCE THEY SUBMIT PROOF THAT THE GOODS HAVE BEEN SHIPPED." The bank steps in as a trusted middleman | | BILL OF LADING | "The delivery receipt for goods in shipping", issued by the shipping company (e.g. Maersk), confirming the goods have been loaded. It ALSO ACTS AS A TITLE OF OWNERSHIP — whoever holds it legally OWNS the goods guaranteed MCQ| | COMMERCIAL INVOICE | A detailed bill from exporter to importer — what is sold, value, quantity, payment terms | | CERTIFICATE OF ORIGIN | States WHERE THE GOODS WERE MANUFACTURED — important for customs clearance and trade agreements |

    19.4 THE LETTER OF CREDIT PROCESS — the eight steps guaranteed MCQ

    The four players: the IMPORTER (buyer) · the EXPORTER (seller) · the IMPORTER'S BANK = the ISSUING BANK · the EXPORTER'S BANK = the ADVISING BANK. guaranteed MCQ — these two bank names| Step | Action | |---|---| | 1 | The importer approaches SBI (issuing bank) to request an LC in favour of the German exporter | | 2 | SBI creates the LC and sends it to Deutsche Bank (advising bank) | | 3 | Deutsche Bank VERIFIES ITS AUTHENTICITY and informs the exporter that payment is guaranteed | | 4 | The exporter SHIPS THE GOODS and prepares the documents — commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, inspection certificates | | 5 | The exporter submits the documents to the advising bank, which checks they match the LC terms | | 6 | Deutsche Bank forwards the documents to SBI | | 7 | SBI reviews them; if satisfied, sends them to the importer, who can now claim the goods at the port | | 8 | SBI pays Deutsche Bank → Deutsche Bank pays the exporter |

    19.5 THE COLLECTION PROCESS guaranteed MCQ — do not confuse with the LC

    Different bank names here: the EXPORTER'S bank is the REMITTING BANK; the IMPORTER'S bank is the COLLECTING BANK. guaranteed MCQ Flow: exporter ships goods and submits documents to the REMITTING BANK → remitting bank sends the documents to the COLLECTING BANK (NO FUNDS MOVE AT THIS POINT — just the documents) → the collecting bank shows the documents to the importer → THE IMPORTER PAYS → the documents are RELEASED so the importer can claim the goods from customs → the collecting bank sends the funds back to the remitting bank → the exporter is paid.

    Why use it: "It adds a layer of trust WITHOUT needing a letter of credit. The exporter does not release documents until payment is received. Especially useful in MEDIUM-TRUST relationships — MORE SECURE THAN A DIRECT TRANSFER BUT LESS FORMAL THAN A LETTER OF CREDIT." guaranteed MCQ

    19.6 THE SEVEN CHALLENGES OF TRADITIONAL TRADE FINANCE guaranteed MCQ| # | Challenge | Detail |

    |---|---|---| | 1 | INVOICE FACTORING RISK | An exporter may finance the SAME INVOICE with MULTIPLE BANKS — "like showing the same bill to different people and borrowing from each" | | 2 | MANUAL CONTRACT PROCESSING | Errors, slow turnaround, extra paperwork | | 3 | DELAYED SHIPMENTS AND PAYMENTS | Too many middlemen each doing checks | | 4 | DUPLICATIVE BILLS OF LADING | Paper documents are easy to copy → DUPLICATE FINANCING FRAUD | | 5 | DISPARATE PLATFORMS | Different banks use different IT systems and formats that don't talk to each other | | 6 | VERSION CONTROL | No way to ensure everyone uses the latest version of a contract | | 7 | MANUAL AML REVIEWS | Slow, expensive and prone to human error |

    19.7 The blockchain trade finance ecosystem guaranteed MCQ

    Each party — exporter, importer, export bank, import bank, transporter, insurance company, REGULATORS — has its own NODE in a shared blockchain network (a DISTRIBUTED LEDGER) where everyone sees THE SAME VERIFIED VERSION OF THE TRUTH IN REAL TIME.

    "Think of it like a WHATSAPP GROUP where all parties are on the same chat, updates are instant, visible to everyone and secure."

    19.8 THE FIVE KEY COMPONENTS of blockchain trade finance guaranteed MCQ

    1. SMART CONTRACTS (automate sale contracts, payment obligations, LC conditions — "if the exporter uploads the bill of lading, the contract automatically releases payment") · 2. NO COURIER/EMAIL DELAYS (both banks instantly view and approve, reducing days to minutes) · 3. DIGITAL SIGNATURES (tamper-proof, for exporters, inspectors, banks, insurers) · 4. TRIGGER-BASED PAYMENTS (payment released when the importer acknowledges receipt) · 5. END-TO-END TRANSPARENCY ("a SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH" — regulators, customs and auditors can access the whole trail in real time).

Handles cargo release, trade finance, ELECTRONIC BILL OF LADING (eBL). IMPACT: cargo release time cut from DAYS TO HOURS · improved container turnaround · reduced port congestion · OVER 1 MILLION SHIPMENTS PROCESSED | | MARCO POLO NETWORK | R3 CORDA, operated by TradeIX | BNP Paribas, ING, Commerzbank | Focuses on OPEN ACCOUNT TRADE (goods shipped BEFORE payment). Features: payment commitment · receivables financing · real-time data sharing | | we.trade | IBM HYPERLEDGER FABRIC | HSBC, UniCredit, Santander | Smart contract services · bank payment guarantees · AUTOMATIC SETTLEMENT when goods are delivered · INVOICE FINANCING for small businesses |

    Real-time review · complete transparency (invoices are visible and TIMESTAMPED, reducing DOUBLE FINANCING) · DISINTERMEDIATION · avoids DOUBLE SPENDING and duplicate claims · trust between strangers · smart contracts automate compliance checks and payment triggers · PROOF OF OWNERSHIP tracked digitally · reduced transaction cost (especially for SMALL AND MEDIUM EXPORTERS facing high banking fees) · regulators get real-time compliance data.

    1. DIGITAL IDENTITY, KYC AND SELF-SOVEREIGN IDENTITY guaranteed MCQ
    12

    20.1 Digital identity — the definition

    "A set of DATA that UNIQUELY IDENTIFIES a person, an ORGANISATION, an APPLICATION or a DEVICE on the internet."

    Attributes: full name, date of birth, home address · employment history (LinkedIn) · BROWSING HISTORY · SOCIAL MEDIA ACTIVITY · FINANCIAL INFORMATION (credit score, past transactions).

    WHO/WHAT HAS A DIGITAL IDENTITY — the four categories: guaranteed MCQ 1. INDIVIDUALS · 2. DEVICES (phones, laptops, home gadgets — tracked by IP or MAC addresses) · 3. ORGANISATIONS (companies, government offices, NGOs) · 4. SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS AND APIs.

    20.2 KYC — the definition guaranteed MCQ

    "The MANDATORY process of IDENTIFYING and VERIFYING a client's identity WHEN OPENING AN ACCOUNT and PERIODICALLY OVER TIME."

    Purpose: stop criminals from opening fake accounts, committing fraud or laundering money.

    20.3 THE FOUR STEPS OF TRADITIONAL KYC guaranteed MCQ

    1. IDENTITY VERIFICATION (at account opening) · 2. CUSTOMER DUE DILIGENCE (gather more info to assess risk) · 3. ENHANCED DUE DILIGENCE (for HIGH-RISK customers, reviewing past financial behaviour) · 4. CONTINUOUS MONITORING ("KYC is NOT a one-time thing").

    20.4 The three-party model guaranteed MCQ| Party | Role |

    |---|---| | ISSUERS | Organisations that give you official documents or identity proofs — the passport department, a university degree, a training certificate | | HOLDER | YOU — storing them as PDFs, in DigiLocker, or physically | | VERIFIERS | A bank, an employer, an online store offering credit — who need to check the credentials |

    20.5 THE COST AND TIME OF TRADITIONAL KYC guaranteed MCQ — the numbers| Metric | Figure |

    |---|---| | Cost per KYC verification | ₹100 to ₹500 — and it is REPEATED every time, at every institution | | Time to onboard a client | 5 to 10 days, sometimes 2–3 weeks | | Manual work involved | around 50 HOURS |

    The other challenges: customer frustration at repeated requests · inaccurate data → non-compliance, fines and legal issues · hard to access INTERNATIONAL business data · DATA STORED IN SILOS ("the PF department doesn't speak to the bank; the bank doesn't speak to the insurer").

    "A corporate client might be asked for the SAME PAN and GST details FIVE TIMES BY FIVE DIFFERENT DEPARTMENTS IN THE SAME BANK." guaranteed MCQ

    20.6 SELF-SOVEREIGN IDENTITY (SSI) guaranteed MCQ

    "SSI means YOU are the OWNER of your digital identity — NOT your bank, NOT the government, NOT a tech company. You own the verifiable digital identity, stored securely, and YOU DECIDE WHO CAN ACCESS YOUR KYC DATA."

    THE FOUR STEPS OF BLOCKCHAIN KYC: guaranteed MCQ| Step | Action | |---|---| | 1 | The customer uploads KYC documents (Aadhaar, PAN, proof of address, passport) to a secure digital platform connected to the blockchain | | 2 | One bank performs the KYC ONCE, verifies, and labels the customer KYC-compliant | | 3 | CRITICAL: the ACTUAL DOCUMENTS ARE NOT STORED ON THE BLOCKCHAIN — only a CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROOF of the KYC is stored guaranteed MCQ| | 4 | A new institution (Axis Bank, Zerodha, an HDFC loan) requests access; the customer GRANTS PERMISSION; they VERIFY THE KYC STATUS ON THE BLOCKCHAIN instantly — no re-upload, no waiting, no repeated checks |

    The technical trio: ISSUER (creates VERIFIABLE CREDENTIALS, digitally signed and stored on a public blockchain to confirm authenticity WITHOUT REVEALING PERSONAL DATA) → HOLDER (stores them in a DIGITAL IDENTITY WALLET on their phone or cloud) → VERIFIER (sends a PROOF REQUEST; the holder approves and SHARES ONLY WHAT IS NECESSARY). guaranteed MCQ The public blockchain acts as "a TRUST LAYER — a decentralised, tamper-proof registry that stores ONLY VERIFIED DATA, NOT personal files."

    20.7 THE INDIAN BLOCKCHAIN KYC PILOT guaranteed MCQ — the whole box

    "ONE KYC, MANY USERS." WHO: SEBI (India's capital market regulator) ran a pilot for INVESTOR ONBOARDING using blockchain-based KYC. BUILT BY: INFOSYS and TCS, using blockchain frameworks like HYPERLEDGER. PARTICIPATING BANKS: SBI, AXIS BANK and YES BANK. THE RESULTS: - 60% to 80% COST REDUCTION for banks - Onboarding time reduced from DAYS TO MINUTES - Better compliance and audit tracking

    The benefits summarised: FASTER onboarding · MORE SECURE (no data actually stored) · HIGHLY PRIVATE (only the PROOF is shared, not the documents) · NO FAKES · NO DELAYS · NO REPEATED KYC.

    PART B — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

    1. AI fundamentals
    7

    21.1 What AI is guaranteed MCQ

    "The ability of MACHINES to perform tasks that typically require HUMAN INTELLIGENCE — learning from data, recognising patterns, understanding language, making decisions and ADAPTING OVER TIME."

    The four capabilities he lists: SEE (facial recognition) · HEAR AND SPEAK (voice assistants) · READ AND WRITE (chatbots) · THINK AND LEARN (recommendation systems, fraud detectors).

    In FinTech: evaluate loan applications · detect suspicious transactions · personalise investment strategy · help banks comply with regulations — "all at speed and scale humans alone just can't match."

    21.2 ANI vs AGI guaranteed MCQ| | ANI — Artificial NARROW Intelligence | AGI — Artificial GENERAL Intelligence |

    |---|---|---| | Also called | WEAK AI | STRONG AI | | Definition | Designed to perform a SPECIFIC TASK — and does one task really well | HUMAN-LEVEL intelligence — able to understand, learn and apply knowledge ACROSS A WIDE RANGE of tasks | | Examples | A chatbot answering queries · an algorithm approving loans · a fraud detection system | DOES NOT EXIST YET — it is still a goal for the future | | Analogy | "Like a TOOL" | "Like a HUMAN BRAIN IN A MACHINE" |

    21.3 The AI → ML → DL nesting guaranteed MCQ

    AI is the LARGEST circle — any technique enabling computers to MIMIC human intelligence. Within AI is MACHINE LEARNING — algorithms that let systems LEARN FROM DATA and improve over time WITHOUT being explicitly programmed for every scenario. Within ML is DEEP LEARNING — using complex NEURAL NETWORKS inspired by the human brain, especially powerful with large-scale data like images, speech or financial transaction patterns.

    "ALL deep learning is machine learning, and ALL machine learning is AI — but NOT ALL AI IS MACHINE LEARNING." guaranteed MCQ

    21.4 TOM MITCHELL'S DEFINITION OF MACHINE LEARNING guaranteed MCQ — the exact wording

    "A computer program is said to LEARN from EXPERIENCE E with respect to some TASK T and some PERFORMANCE MEASURE P, if its performance at task T, as measured by P, IMPROVES WITH EXPERIENCE E." — Tom Mitchell

    The fraud-detection mapping: guaranteed MCQ - TASK T = detecting whether a credit card transaction is fraudulent - EXPERIENCE E = the data set of past transactions labelled fraudulent or not fraudulent - PERFORMANCE MEASURE P = accuracy or a metric like the F1 SCORE on a test data set

    21.5 THE THREE REASONS TO USE MACHINE LEARNING guaranteed MCQ| # | Reason | Detail |

    |---|---|---| | 1 | The LIMITATIONS OF THE TRADITIONAL APPROACH | Traditional programmers write explicit rules for every situation ("if the amount > ₹1,00,000 and the location is foreign, flag it"). But there are thousands of SUBTLE PATTERNS humans can't define with clear rules | | 2 | AUTOMATICALLY ADAPTING TO CHANGE | Customer behaviour, fraud tactics and market conditions constantly change. A traditional system needs MANUAL updates; an ML model retrains on new data | | 3 | MACHINE LEARNING CAN HELP HUMANS LEARN | Models uncover hidden patterns analysts may not have noticed — e.g. "a sudden spike in online spending is linked to a future loan default." ML doesn't just AUTOMATE decisions, it AUGMENTS human intelligence |

    1. The three learning mechanisms guaranteed MCQ
    4

    22.1 SUPERVISED LEARNING

    "The model is trained on a LABELLED data set — for each input we already know the correct output. LABELS are the known outcomes or targets associated with each data point."

    Sub-type Label type FinTech examples
    CLASSIFICATION CATEGORICAL — the label belongs to a specific class or group Fraud detection (amount, location, time, device used → fraudulent / not fraudulent) · loan approval (approve / reject) · KYC verification (classifying users as LOW RISK or HIGH RISK)
    REGRESSION NUMERICAL — predicting a CONTINUOUS value Credit scoring (from income, repayment history, credit utilisation) · stock price prediction · customer lifetime value · estimating the interest rate to offer a borrower

    22.2 UNSUPERVISED LEARNING

    "Trained on data that has NO LABELLED OUTPUTS. We don't tell the model the correct answers — the algorithm tries to DISCOVER HIDDEN PATTERNS, STRUCTURES OR RELATIONSHIPS on its own."

    When to use it: guaranteed MCQ - When labelling data is too costly or time-consuming - When you want to explore the data to find natural groupings - When the goal is EXPLORATION OR DISCOVERY rather than PREDICTION

    Sub-type Detail
    CLUSTERING The most common type. Groups data points by similarity. Named algorithms: K-MEANS, DBSCAN, HIERARCHICAL clustering. The customer-segmentation example produces segments like high-income low-risk investors · young high-spending users · low-balance high-frequency transaction users
    DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION Simplifying data sets with many features while retaining the most important information. PCA — PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS reduces hundreds of features to two or three dimensions for visualisation; also speeds up processing and reduces noise

    22.3 REINFORCEMENT LEARNING guaranteed MCQ

    "An AGENT learns by INTERACTING with an ENVIRONMENT, taking ACTIONS and receiving REWARDS or PENALTIES based on outcomes." The FinTech example: ALGORITHMIC TRADING — a trading agent learns to buy or sell based on market movements, getting REWARDS for profitable trades and PENALTIES for losses, learning to MAXIMISE LONG-TERM RETURNS. The key feature: LEARNING THROUGH TRIAL AND ERROR, "like training a robot or playing a game."

    THE ONE-LINE SUMMARY: guaranteed MCQ

    "SUPERVISED is like teaching WITH ANSWER KEYS. UNSUPERVISED is about DISCOVERING HIDDEN PATTERNS. REINFORCEMENT is about learning FROM INTERACTION AND FEEDBACK."

    1. Regression
    17

    23.1 Simple linear regression guaranteed MCQ

    Loan amount = W × monthly income + B

    Term Meaning
    Monthly income The INPUT FEATURE, also called the INDEPENDENT VARIABLE
    Loan amount The TARGET / OUTPUT, also called the DEPENDENT VARIABLE
    W The WEIGHT or SLOPE — how much the output increases per unit of input
    B The BIAS or INTERCEPT — the baseline

    THE WORKED EXAMPLE: Loan amount = 4 × monthly income + 20,000 guaranteed MCQ - "For every extra dollar someone earns monthly, their eligible loan increases by $4" - "Even with ZERO income, the model suggests a base loan of $20,000 — that's the INTERCEPT" - Income $50,000 → 4 × 50,000 + 20,000 = $220,000

    23.2 MULTIPLE linear regression — the worked example guaranteed MCQ — every coefficient

    Loan amount = 4 × income + 200 × credit score − 1.5 × EMI + 10,000

    Term Interpretation
    4 × income For every $1 increase in monthly income, the predicted loan rises $4 (holding others constant)
    200 × credit score For every 1-point increase in credit score, the predicted loan rises $200
    −1.5 × EMI For every $1 increase in existing EMI, the predicted loan FALLS $1.50
    +10,000 The intercept — the baseline when all inputs are zero

    THE WORKED CALCULATION: income $5,000, credit score 700, EMI $1,000 = 4(5,000) + 200(700) − 1.5(1,000) + 10,000 = 20,000 + 140,000 − 1,500 + 10,000 = $168,500 guaranteed MCQ (Credit score ranges from 300 to 850 in this example.)

    23.3 THE FOUR REGRESSION EVALUATION METRICS guaranteed MCQ

    WHY RAW ERROR FAILS — the worked demonstration: guaranteed MCQ

    Case 1: actual 90, predicted 100 → error +10. Case 2: actual 110, predicted 100 → error −10. Average the two and you get ZERO — "it looks like the model made NO ERROR AT ALL, but that's clearly not true. The model was wrong BOTH times, just in opposite directions."

    Metric Formula idea Character
    MAE — MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR Average of the ABSOLUTE values of the errors "How far, on average, the predictions are from the actual values, without positive and negative errors cancelling out"
    MSE — MEAN SQUARED ERROR SQUARES the errors before averaging Penalises LARGER mistakes MORE HEAVILY; ensures all errors are positive. Downside: the result is in SQUARED UNITS — dollars squared — which is hard to interpret
    RMSE — ROOT MEAN SQUARED ERROR The SQUARE ROOT of the MSE In the SAME UNIT as the predicted value, and still penalises large errors — "one of the most popular evaluation metrics for regression"
    R² (R-SQUARED) 1 − (total squared error ÷ total variance in the actual data) "What PERCENTAGE OF THE VARIANCE in the target variable is EXPLAINED BY THE MODEL." R² = 1 → perfect prediction. R² = 0 → NO BETTER THAN JUST PREDICTING THE AVERAGE EVERY TIME guaranteed MCQ

    23.4 THE NORMAL EQUATION guaranteed MCQ

    W = (Xᵀ X)⁻¹ Xᵀ y "A CLOSED-FORM solution — a DIRECT FORMULA to calculate the optimal weights. NO ITERATIONS NEEDED."

    Symbol Meaning
    X The matrix of input features — each ROW is a training example, each COLUMN a feature
    y The vector of actual output values
    Xᵀ The transpose of X

    WHEN IT WORKS AND WHEN IT DOESN'T: guaranteed MCQ

    "It works great when the number of features is SMALL and the data is not too large. But as the data set grows, especially with THOUSANDS OF FEATURES, computing the INVERSE of XᵀX becomes VERY SLOW AND MEMORY-INTENSIVE. That's when we switch to iterative methods like GRADIENT DESCENT."

    23.5 GRADIENT DESCENT guaranteed MCQ

    THE MOUNTAIN ANALOGY: "You are standing somewhere on a mountain BLINDFOLDED. Your goal is to reach the lowest point in the valley. Since you can't see, you FEEL THE SLOPE beneath your feet and take a small step in the direction sloping downward the most. Repeat until the ground is flat."

    The mapping: the MOUNTAIN is the COST FUNCTION (e.g. MSE); the LOWEST POINT is where the model performs best.

    The four steps: 1. Start with RANDOM weights → 2. Calculate the LOSS → 3. The GRADIENT tells us the direction and rate of change of that loss → 4. Take a step in the OPPOSITE direction of the gradient (because we want to REDUCE the loss).

    WHY IT WORKS RELIABLY FOR LINEAR REGRESSION: guaranteed MCQ

    "For linear regression the cost function (MSE) is a CONVEX function — shaped like a nice smooth BOWL — so there is only ONE GLOBAL MINIMUM. No matter where you start, if you step carefully, you'll eventually reach that lowest point." BUT for NEURAL NETWORKS the landscape is NOT smooth — it has MULTIPLE VALLEYS, and gradient descent can get STUCK IN A LOCAL MINIMUM. Remedies: RESTART training from different random points, or use advanced methods.

    THE LEARNING RATE: guaranteed MCQ

    "If the learning rate is TOO SMALL, the model learns very slowly — it takes forever. If TOO LARGE, the model might OVERSHOOT the minimum, bounce around and never settle, or even DIVERGE." "Like choosing the right step size when climbing down a mountain — too small and you crawl, too big and you might trip and fall."

    23.6 THE THREE TYPES OF GRADIENT DESCENT guaranteed MCQ — the whole table| Type | How it works | Pros | Cons |

    |---|---|---|---| | BATCH gradient descent | Uses the ENTIRE training data set to compute the gradient before any weight update | Stable, smooth descent | SLOW with large data sets | | STOCHASTIC gradient descent (SGD) | Updates the weights after looking at JUST ONE training example at a time, randomly chosen. "STOCHASTIC means RANDOM" | Much faster updates · helps with real-time training · CAN ESCAPE LOCAL MINIMA in non-convex problems due to the randomness · you see learning progress early | NOISY — the loss jumps up and down; may not converge smoothly; needs careful learning-rate tuning, momentum or LR schedules | | MINI-BATCH gradient descent | Splits the data into small batches — 32, 64 or 128 examples | THE MOST WIDELY USED IN PRACTICE. Faster than batch, more stable than SGD, leverages GPU hardware acceleration and VECTORISATION | Needs experimentation with batch size and LR; must handle non-divisible data sets (padding or dropping the last batch); needs SHUFFLING so mini-batches are representative |

    The walking analogy: guaranteed MCQ

    "BATCH gradient descent is someone walking SLOWLY AND STEADILY downhill with full knowledge of the terrain. STOCHASTIC gradient descent is someone taking FAST ZIGZAG STEPS, reacting immediately to the ground beneath each foot — sometimes stepping in the wrong direction, but ON AVERAGE getting closer to the bottom."

    The one-line summary: "BATCH is SLOW BUT STABLE. STOCHASTIC is FAST BUT NOISY. MINI-BATCH is the SWEET SPOT — the method of choice for deep learning today."

    23.7 Two hyperparameters introduced here guaranteed MCQ| Term | Definition |

    |---|---| | HYPERPARAMETER | "A setting that YOU, THE MODEL DESIGNER, CHOOSE BEFORE TRAINING BEGINS. Unlike MODEL PARAMETERS (weights and biases) which are LEARNED FROM DATA, hyperparameters are SET MANUALLY." | | EPOCH | "ONE FULL CYCLE THROUGH THE ENTIRE TRAINING DATA SET" — the model sees and learns from every example once. Too many epochs may not help and could make performance on new data WORSE |

    Common batch sizes: 32, 64, 128. Smaller batches → NOISIER but MORE FREQUENT updates. Larger batches → MORE STABLE but SLOWER per update.

    23.8 POLYNOMIAL REGRESSION guaranteed MCQ

    The motivating example: predicting customer SPENDING by AGE — "young adults spend moderately, middle-aged people spend more, older customers spend less." That is a CURVE, not a straight line.

    The mountain-road analogy: "If you only have straight roads in your GPS, you either UNDERFIT the curves or OVERSHOOT them entirely."

    Polynomial regression is STILL A LINEAR MODEL — but instead of just X, we include POWERS OF X as additional features (X², X³, … up to degree D). We are still using a LINEAR EQUATION IN THE WEIGHTS, but on TRANSFORMED INPUT VARIABLES. guaranteed MCQ The worked quadratic: y = 0.5x² + 1.2x − 2 + noise

    Why use it: 1. fit curves in clearly non-linear data · 2. improve accuracy without switching algorithms · 3. PRESERVE INTERPRETABILITY, especially at lower degrees.

    1. Data splitting, fitting and regularisation
    8

    24.1 THE THREE DATA SPLITS guaranteed MCQ — the percentages| Set | Purpose | Typical share |

    |---|---|---| | TRAINING set | The only part the model SEES while learning | 62–70% | | VALIDATION set | Evaluate on unseen data to tune settings (e.g. polynomial degree), decide when to stop training, and compare models — "a mini test to guide us while still in the development phase" | 15–20% | | TEST set | Data the model has NEVER SEEN AT ANY POINT — gives a realistic estimate of real-world performance | 15–20% |

    THE REAL-WORLD PRACTICE HE FLAGS: guaranteed MCQ

    "In industry projects or client engagements, we often only split into TRAINING and VALIDATION on our side, with an 80/20 or 70/30 ratio. THE TEST DATA SET IS HELD BACK BY THE CLIENT and used by them to INDEPENDENTLY evaluate the model, especially when the model will be deployed on confidential or sensitive data they can't share."

    Why split at all: "If we evaluate the model on the SAME DATA WE TRAINED IT ON, WE ARE FOOLING OURSELVES."

    24.2 UNDERFITTING, GOOD FIT, OVERFITTING guaranteed MCQ — the loss-curve signatures| Scenario | Definition | Training loss | Validation loss | Loss curve signature |

    |---|---|---|---|---| | UNDERFITTING | The model is TOO SIMPLE to capture the underlying pattern — e.g. predicting house prices using ONLY the number of bedrooms, ignoring location, square footage, age | HIGH | HIGH | Both curves stay FAR FROM ZERO and CLOSE TOGETHER — "the model is underpowered" | | GOOD FIT | Just enough complexity to capture the structure without memorising | Decreases steadily | Follows along, then flattens | Both come down and STAY TOGETHER at a relatively low point | | OVERFITTING | The model becomes TOO GOOD AT MEMORISING the training data, including NOISE AND OUTLIERS — e.g. including "the number of windows, the colour of the roof, the direction the main door faces" | Keeps dropping, maybe approaching ZERO | STARTS INCREASING after a point | THE GAP between training and validation loss is the OVERFITTING ZONE |

    FIXING UNDERFITTING: add more relevant variables/weights. FIXING OVERFITTING — the two simple fixes: guaranteed MCQ 1. REDUCE MODEL COMPLEXITY — FEWER PARAMETERS (reduce the polynomial degree; drop irrelevant/redundant features) 2. ADD MORE DATA — MORE ROWS, NOT COLUMNS. "Overfitting is like a student who memorises a short set of practice questions and aces a test only because they got lucky. Give them a LARGER, MORE DIVERSE question bank and they're forced to actually learn the concept."

    24.3 REGULARISATION guaranteed MCQ

    "A technique that prevents overfitting by ADDING A PENALTY TO THE COST FUNCTION. This discourages the model from relying too heavily on LARGE WEIGHTS. So instead of just minimising prediction error, the model ALSO has to keep its weights small and controlled."

    Used when "you WANT to keep the model complex — say a polynomial model or one with many features — AND still avoid overfitting."

    L2 — RIDGE REGRESSION L1 — LASSO REGRESSION
    Penalty added The SUM OF THE SQUARES of the weights (the L2 norm) The SUM OF THE ABSOLUTE VALUES of the weights (the L1 norm)
    Effect on weights SHRINKS the weights but does NOT ELIMINATE them — keeps ALL features, with less impact Drives some weights ALL THE WAY DOWN TO ZERO — effectively performing FEATURE SELECTION guaranteed MCQ
    Analogy "Like a SPRING pulling the weights toward zero — the more they stretch, the harder the pullback" Ignores unhelpful features completely
    When to use When you think MANY features contribute A LITTLE When you believe ONLY A FEW features really matter

    λ (LAMBDA) is the REGULARISATION PARAMETER — it controls HOW MUCH PENALTY we add. guaranteed MCQ Combining both: ELASTIC NET — "a mix of both L1 and L2 regularisation." guaranteed MCQ "Regularisation is like giving your model a CONSTRAINT: you are ALLOWED TO LEARN, but DON'T GET TOO CARRIED AWAY."

    1. Classification
    19

    25.1 The three types of classification guaranteed MCQ| Type | Definition | FinTech example |

    |---|---|---| | BINARY | TWO classes | Will the customer default — yes or no? | | MULTI-CLASS | MORE than two classes | What is the customer's credit rating — A, B, C or D? | | MULTI-LABEL | ASSIGN MULTIPLE LABELS to each input | Tagging a financial article as investing, banking OR economy |

    "Instead of a LINE, now we are drawing BOUNDARIES between different groups."

    The named algorithms: LOGISTIC REGRESSION · DECISION TREES · ENSEMBLE TECHNIQUES (random forest, boosting) · NEURAL NETWORKS.

    25.2 LOGISTIC REGRESSION guaranteed MCQ

    WHY NOT JUST USE LINEAR REGRESSION WITH A THRESHOLD? guaranteed MCQ

    "Linear regression can output ANY value from NEGATIVE INFINITY TO POSITIVE INFINITY. But in classification we want a prediction BETWEEN 0 AND 1, something we can interpret as a PROBABILITY."

    Logistic regression passes the output of the linear model through the LOGISTIC (or SIGMOID) FUNCTION, which squeezes the result into a curve between 0 and 1. Where Z = W₀ + W₁X₁ + W₂X₂ + … + WₙXₙ "No matter what value of Z we get, the output of the sigmoid is ALWAYS between 0 and 1."

    The threshold: typically 0.5. If P ≥ 0.5 → class 1. If P < 0.5 → class 0.

    Despite the name, LOGISTIC REGRESSION IS USED FOR CLASSIFICATION, NOT REGRESSION. guaranteed MCQ

    25.3 LOG LOSS / BINARY CROSS-ENTROPY guaranteed MCQ

    "We need a loss function that REWARDS the model when it assigns high probability to the correct class and PENALISES IT HEAVILY when it is CONFIDENT BUT WRONG." Where y is the actual label (0 or 1) and p is the predicted probability that the label is 1.

    The interpretation: guaranteed MCQ - True label 1, predicted close to 1 → SMALL loss (good) - True label 1, predicted 0.01 → VERY LARGE loss, "because the model was CONFIDENTLY WRONG"

    "Log loss is ASYMMETRICAL and SHARP. It heavily penalises confident wrong predictions and gently rewards correct ones. It is designed to optimise PROBABILITIES, not just class labels — it pushes the model to be CONFIDENT WHEN IT'S RIGHT and CAUTIOUS WHEN IT'S UNCERTAIN."

    25.4 SOFTMAX REGRESSION guaranteed MCQ

    "Also known as MULTINOMIAL LOGISTIC REGRESSION — the MULTI-CLASS EXTENSION of logistic regression. Instead of predicting just one probability, it predicts a PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION ACROSS MULTIPLE CLASSES and picks the one with the highest probability." The SOFTMAX function converts scores into probability values that ALL ADD UP TO 1. "Softmax AMPLIFIES the highest score and PUSHES DOWN the rest."

    The worked example: 10% low risk · 20% medium risk · 70% HIGH RISK → the model picks HIGH RISK. guaranteed MCQ Its loss function: CATEGORICAL CROSS-ENTROPY — "just like log loss, but extended across multiple classes." guaranteed MCQ "Think of Softmax as logistic regression, but with MORE THAN TWO DOORS to choose from."

    25.5 THE DECISION BOUNDARY guaranteed MCQ

    "The imaginary LINE or SURFACE (in higher dimensions) that SPLITS THE FEATURE SPACE so the model knows which region corresponds to which class. It is WHERE THE MODEL FLIPS ITS DECISION." In logistic regression it is LINEAR — a straight line or plane — and it comes from THE POINT WHERE THE MODEL OUTPUT EQUALS 0.5. "That's where the model is UNSURE, right on the edge."

    For NON-linearly-separable data: POLYNOMIAL LOGISTIC REGRESSION (curved boundaries) · DECISION TREES (STEP-LIKE boundaries) · NEURAL NETWORKS (very flexible, "even weird-looking" boundaries). guaranteed MCQ

    25.6 THE CONFUSION MATRIX guaranteed MCQ| Term | Definition |

    |---|---| | TRUE POSITIVE (TP) | The model correctly predicts a POSITIVE case | | TRUE NEGATIVE (TN) | The model correctly predicts a NEGATIVE case | | FALSE POSITIVE (FP) | The model incorrectly predicts positive — A FALSE ALARM | | FALSE NEGATIVE (FN) | The model MISSES a positive case |

    THE WORKED FRAUD EXAMPLE — memorise these four numbers: guaranteed MCQ| Quantity | Value | |---|---| | TP (frauds correctly detected) | 90 | | FN (frauds missed) | 10 | | FP (good transactions falsely flagged) | 20 | | TN (good transactions correctly allowed) | 880 | | Total | 1,000 |

    Metric Formula Calculation Result
    ACCURACY (TP + TN) ÷ total (90 + 880) ÷ 1,000 ≈ 97%
    PRECISION TP ÷ (TP + FP) — "Out of all the cases the model PREDICTED as fraud, how many WERE actually fraud?" 90 ÷ 110 ≈ 81.8%
    RECALL TP ÷ (TP + FN) — "Out of all the ACTUAL frauds, how many did the model CATCH?" 90 ÷ 100 90%
    F1 SCORE 2 × (precision × recall) ÷ (precision + recall) — the HARMONIC MEAN ≈ 85.7%

    25.7 THE CLASS IMBALANCE TRAP guaranteed MCQ — a certain exam item

    "Only 1% of transactions are actually fraudulent. Out of 10,000 transactions, 100 are fraud and 9,900 are legitimate. Now imagine you build a model that predicts EVERY transaction as NOT FRAUD — it does nothing clever. But it will be 99% ACCURATE, because it gets 9,900 out of 10,000 right. IT LOOKS GREAT ON PAPER, BUT IT IS USELESS — IT MISSED ALL THE FRAUD CASES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE MODEL."

    Therefore in imbalanced data sets, use PRECISION, RECALL and F1 — NOT ACCURACY.

    25.8 The precision–recall trade-off guaranteed MCQ

    "Lower the decision threshold from 0.5 to 0.3 and you'll CATCH MORE FRAUDS (HIGHER RECALL), but you'll also flag more transactions as fraud (LOWER PRECISION)." - Building a FRAUD DETECTION system → prefer HIGHER RECALL ("you'd rather catch more fraud, even at the cost of some false alarms") - Building an INSTANT PAYMENTS APPROVAL system → PRECISION matters more ("you don't want to wrongly block legitimate users")

    25.9 THE ROC CURVE AND AUC guaranteed MCQ

    ROC = RECEIVER OPERATING CHARACTERISTIC. It shows how well a model can separate classes ACROSS ALL CLASSIFICATION THRESHOLDS. Y-AXIS: TRUE POSITIVE RATE (TPR), also known as RECALL. X-AXIS: FALSE POSITIVE RATE (FPR). Each POINT on the curve corresponds to a DIFFERENT THRESHOLD. - A PERFECT model shoots up to the TOP LEFT CORNER — high TPR, low FPR - A RANDOM GUESSER lies along the DIAGONAL line

    AUC — AREA UNDER THE CURVE: guaranteed MCQ

    "A single number summarising the ROC curve. It tells you THE PROBABILITY THAT THE MODEL WILL RANK A RANDOMLY CHOSEN POSITIVE INSTANCE HIGHER THAN A RANDOMLY CHOSEN NEGATIVE ONE."

    AUC value Meaning
    1.0 A PERFECT classifier
    0.5 NO BETTER THAN RANDOM GUESSING
    < 0.5 WORSE than random — "it usually means something is wrong"

    The threshold illustration: at 0.9 → HIGH PRECISION but LOW RECALL (you miss many frauds). At 0.3 → catch more frauds (HIGH RECALL) but flag many good users (LOW PRECISION).

    25.10 HANDLING IMBALANCED CLASSES — the two strategies guaranteed MCQ| Strategy | Method | Detail |

    |---|---|---| | 1. RESAMPLING | OVERSAMPLING | Increase the MINORITY class by duplicating existing fraud cases or SYNTHESISING new ones. The named technique: SMOTE — SYNTHETIC MINORITY OVERSAMPLING TECHNIQUE, which "generates NEW, SLIGHTLY VARIED SYNTHETIC EXAMPLES based on existing minority data" guaranteed MCQ| | | UNDERSAMPLING | Reduce the MAJORITY class. "Works well if you have a huge data set, but it might THROW AWAY USEFUL INFORMATION" | | 2. CLASS WEIGHTING / COST-SENSITIVE LEARNING | Assign HIGHER WEIGHTS to the minority class in the LOSS FUNCTION | "Tell the algorithm: these fraud cases are rare but really important, pay more attention to them." Supported directly by LOGISTIC REGRESSION, RANDOM FOREST and XGBOOST. The model is penalised MORE for misclassifying a fraud case |

    "Often the best results come from a COMBINATION — a bit of oversampling PLUS class weighting, tuned carefully."

    1. Decision trees and ensembles
    36

    26.1 Why decision trees guaranteed MCQ

    "Linear and logistic regression ASSUME the relationship between inputs and output is LINEAR or smoothly curved. But what if the data is more like IF THIS, THEN THAT? Decision trees DON'T try to fit a line or a curve — they take a completely different approach, one that feels MUCH MORE HUMAN. Instead of fitting an equation, a decision tree asks A SERIES OF YES/NO QUESTIONS."

    THE CREDIT APPROVAL WORKED EXAMPLE — memorise the thresholds: guaranteed MCQ

    Is the CREDIT SCORE ≥ 650? If NO → REJECT. If YES → Is the MONTHLY INCOME ≥ $4,000? If NO → REJECT. If YES → Is the LOAN AMOUNT < $20,000? If YES → APPROVE. If NO → Any PAST DEFAULTS? If YES → REJECT. If NO → APPROVE. "Step by step, just like a human loan officer might."

    The advantages: RULE-BASED format is easy to understand and explain · handles NON-LINEAR combinations of features · handles NUMBERS, CATEGORIES OR BOTH without pre-processing · TRANSPARENT — "you can literally walk someone through the decision path."

    26.2 THE THREE STEPS OF BUILDING A TREE guaranteed MCQ| Step | Detail |

    |---|---| | 1. START AT THE ROOT | The ROOT NODE is the very first decision point, containing ALL the training data. The feature is chosen using a SPLITTING CRITERION (gini, entropy, or variance for regression). The goal: the PUREST SUBSETS. This is called DIVIDE AND CONQUER | | 2. SPLIT THE DATA | Creates BRANCHES (EDGES) connecting to the next set of NODES, each with a subset of data. The process repeats RECURSIVELY — each new node becomes its own root | | 3. KEEP SPLITTING UNTIL LEAF NODES | A LEAF is where the model makes its final prediction. Classification trees: each leaf outputs a CLASS LABEL. Regression trees: each leaf outputs a NUMERICAL VALUE — typically the AVERAGE of the data points in that leaf guaranteed MCQ|
